title: Memory between runs
intro: A new run starts with a new messages list. Anything only stored in the old list is gone. To keep a fact across runs, your program writes it outside the list, here to a SQLite file.

steps.author: system
steps.label: System
steps.text: Use short snake_case keys, like editor. remember(key, value) and recall(key).
steps.narration: The system message names the key convention. Both runs see the same instruction, so remember and recall can use the same key.

steps.author: user
steps.label: User
steps.text: Remember that my editor is Helix.
steps.narration: The user asks to store a preference. That sentence lives only in this run's messages until a tool writes it out.

steps.author: model
steps.label: Tool call
steps.narration: The model returns a remember tool call with key editor and value Helix. It cannot write the database itself.

steps.author: tool
steps.label: Tool result
steps.narration: Your program writes the row to memory.db next to this script, then appends that result to this run's list.

steps.author: system
steps.label: New run
steps.text: This is a new message list. Use recall(key) with the same short snake_case keys, like editor.
steps.narration: The next run_agent call starts a new, empty list. memory.db still has the row. The system message still names the key.

steps.author: user
steps.label: User
steps.narration: The question is in this new list. The answer is not, unless the model calls recall with the same key.

steps.author: model
steps.label: Tool call
steps.narration: The model returns a recall tool call for the editor key, the name the system message gave it.

steps.author: tool
steps.label: Tool result
steps.narration: recall returns Helix, or 'no memory found for that key' if the key never matched. Append that to this run's list so the next model call can read it.

steps.author: model
steps.label: Assistant
steps.narration: The model answers from that tool result, not from the previous conversation, which this list does not contain.
